Clinical details: Severe symptomatic aortic stenosis, NYHA II. Heart team referral for TAVI work-up.

Technique: ECG-gated CT angiography of the aortic root and heart, followed by non-gated CT angiography from the thoracic inlet to the lesser trochanters. 75 ml iohexol 350. DLP 612 mGy·cm.

Findings:

Thoracic aorta: Ascending aorta 34 mm. Arch and descending thoracic aorta of normal calibre. No dissection. Mild arch atheroma.

Subclavian/axillary arteries: Unremarkable. No significant stenosis.

Abdominal aorta: Normal calibre. No abdominal aortic aneurysm. Coeliac axis, SMA and renal arteries patent.

Iliofemoral access (minimal luminal diameter):
Right: CIA 8.3 mm, EIA 7.6 mm, CFA 8.0 mm.
Left: CIA 8.1 mm, EIA 7.2 mm, CFA 7.7 mm.
Calcification: mild, non-circumferential. Tortuosity: mild. No dissection or flow-limiting stenosis.

Lungs and airways: No suspicious pulmonary nodule. No consolidation. Airways patent.

Pleura and pericardium: No pleural or pericardial effusion.

Mediastinum: No mediastinal or hilar lymphadenopathy.

Upper abdomen: Unremarkable within the limits of an arterial phase study.

Bones: No aggressive osseous lesion. Degenerative change in the thoracolumbar spine.

Conclusion:
1. Iliofemoral access favourable for a transfemoral approach bilaterally; minimal luminal diameter right 7.6 mm, left 7.2 mm.
2. No significant incidental extracardiac finding.

Annular sizing, valve morphology, coronary ostial heights and aortic root measurements are reported separately in the structural heart report; please refer to that report for valve planning.
